Issued at 155 PM EDT Fri Sep 18 2026

Through Tonight...A mid/upper level low drifting westward towards
the Florida peninsula from the Atlantic has made it to east 
central Florida, with GOES19 visible satellite imagery showing a 
broad counter-clockwise rotation of some upper level clouds. This 
is further supported by SPC upper level analysis, with the 12Z 
analysis indicating the center of the upper level low was just 
offshore. This set-up has brought increasing moisture to the area,
with the dry air mass in the mid-levels slowly being eroded away 
as seen in the observed sounding. Temperatures aloft have also 
cooled a few degrees down to around -10C today as a result of the 
low, as indicated by the 10Z XMR sounding. This set-up combined 
with persistent east- northeast flow at the surface has allowed 
for isolated to scattered showers and storms to develop across the
Atlantic waters this morning and into the early afternoon hours, 
with the diffuse east coast sea breeze supporting further 
development across parts of the Florida peninsula this afternoon. 
Continued development of showers and storms is forecast through 
the remainder of this afternoon, though lingering dry air between 
800-500mb has served as a limiting factor for more robust 
development across the area. This trend will likely continue, with
hi-res guidance continuing to favor lower coverage of activity 
through the rest of today. Trended rain and storm chances slightly
below NBM through this afternoon, with the highest coverage of 
activity anticipated across the Treasure Coast and near Lake 
Okeechobee over the next few hours (40-50%). Given the cold 
temperatures aloft and pocket of lingering dry air in the mid- 
levels, some isolated stronger storms cannot be ruled out across 
east central Florida this afternoon. Storm hazards will include 
frequent lightning strikes, wind gusts up to 50 mph, small hail, 
and heavy rainfall that leads to quick accumulations of 1-3". 
While activity is anticipated to wane into the overnight hours, 
the increasing moisture combined with persistent onshore flow will
continue to support isolated shower and storm development across 
the local Atlantic waters through the overnight hours, with some 
activity potentially moving onshore along the east coast.

Afternoon high temperatures remain on track to range between the 
mid 80s to low 90s, with the warmest temperatures anticipated 
across the far interior northwest of I-4. Tonight, temperatures 
will remain near normal values for this time of year, falling into
the low to mid 70s. A moderate rip current risk persists at the 
local beaches.

Saturday-Sunday...The mid/upper level low will continue to drift 
westward from east central Florida towards the western Florida 
peninsula and the eastern Gulf through Saturday, with the feature 
becoming quasi-stationary on Sunday. This set-up will help keep a 
moist air mass overhead through the weekend, with PWATs forecast 
to range between 1.8-2" on Saturday and exceed 2" areawide on 
Sunday. This moisture combined with persistent northeast flow will
support isolated shower development early in the mornings across 
the local Atlantic waters, with activity drifting onshore. 
Coverage is then anticipated to increase into the afternoon hours 
as a diffuse east coast sea breeze develops and moves inland, with
scattered to numerous showers and storms each day. Some drier air
aloft may help limit coverage on Saturday, so have continued to 
trend slightly below NBM values based on hi-res guidance. Sunday, 
higher coverage of showers is anticipated due to the increasing 
moisture. Isolated to scattered storm development is anticipated 
with activity, especially during the afternoon hours. The low 
overhead combined with daytime heating will create sufficient 
instability across east central Florida, further supported by cold
-8C to -7C 500 mb temperatures. These parameters combined with 
the 1.8-2.0"+ PWATs indicate that primary storm hazards will 
include frequent lightning strikes, wind gusts up to 50 mph, and 
heavy downpours producing quick rainfall accumulations of 1-3". 
Small hail also cannot be fully ruled out given the cooler 
temperatures aloft, but there remains some uncertainty with this. 
Shower and storm activity will gradually diminish across the 
peninsula each evening into the overnight hours, with the 
potential for continued westward-moving shower and storm 
development across the local Atlantic waters. Temperatures are 
forecast to remain seasonable in the upper 80s to low 90s each 
day, with lows in the low to mid 70s each night.

Monday-Thursday...The mid/upper level low will meander across the
eastern Gulf into early next week before lifting northeastward 
and weakening as it is absorbed by a trough pushing across the 
eastern US. Moist air will remain in place across the Florida 
peninsula, with higher rain and storm chances persisting through
